title: Ottawa Street South redevelopment referred over resident displacement
subtitle: Also: affordable housing on Duke Street, two high-rise rezonings on King Street East, and the growth monitoring report.
overview: The committee referred a proposed 20-unit apartment building at 1257-1265 Ottawa Street South to the December 19 Council meeting {{vote:m1}}. Residents of the two houses on the site told the committee they could be displaced and had not heard from the landlord or developer. Staff said the Planning Act gives the city no tools to regulate effects on existing tenants. The referral gives time to ask the developer about relocation and to ask the Region for further comment on traffic.

The committee recommended an eight-storey, 100-unit rental building at Duke Street and Madison Avenue, with 40 deeply affordable units {{vote:m3}}. It also recommended a 27-storey mixed-use building at 1251 King Street East {{vote:m5}}, and a three-tower mixed-use development near the future Sportsworld LRT station, with a corrected floor space ratio of 5.2 {{vote:m6}}. A vacant land condominium for three towers on King Street East received draft approval {{vote:m2}}.
The committee also sent the 2022 growth monitoring report to the Region {{vote:m4}}. Council will make the final decisions on the planning items.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended referring the 20-unit rezoning to the December 19 Council meeting to allow further discussion of options for residents who would be displaced.

decisions.item: 206-210 Duke Street and Madison Avenue North
decisions.detail: The committee recommended adopting the official plan amendment and approving the rezoning for an eight-storey rental building with 40 deeply affordable units near the Kitchener Market LRT station.

decisions.item: 1251 King Street East and 16 Sheldon Avenue South
decisions.detail: The committee recommended adopting the official plan amendment and approving the rezoning to permit a mixed-use development, which staff described as 27 storeys with 408 rental units.

decisions.item: 4220 King Street East and 25 Sportsworld Crossing Road
decisions.detail: The committee recommended approving the amendments for a high-intensity mixed-use development with the floor space ratio set at 5.2, without further public notice.

decisions.item: 3241-3247 King Street East vacant land condominium
decisions.detail: The committee recommended granting draft approval to the vacant land condominium, which is intended to help finance and phase construction of three towers.
The committee decided to submit the 2022 annual monitoring report to the Region of Waterloo, as the delegated approval agreement requires.

debate: On Ottawa Street South, delegates opposed the project because of parking and traffic. They said side streets are already full, the single driveway is on a busy regional road, and one parking space per unit is too few. Staff said the parking rate matches the new zoning by-law and the Region did not require a traffic study.

Neighbours behind the site raised privacy and tree removal. The applicant agreed to an eight-foot fence, though one neighbour said a fence would not stop three storeys of windows from overlooking the yard. Staff said balconies face the street and the rear, and the rear setback is large.

A resident of the Ottawa Street site said they live on a disability support income and could not afford other housing. Councillors asked whether staff or the developer had discussed alternatives. Staff said the Planning Act gives the city no power to regulate the landlord-tenant relationship. One councillor worried that referral could become routine for every application.

On Duke Street, a nearby resident supported the project but described long construction periods and workers parking on side streets. Staff said new site plans require a construction parking plan enforced through the development agreement. Councillors also regretted the drop from 100 to 40 affordable units and raised the need for parkland in the area.

On the Sportsworld Crossing project, the applicant said the floor space ratio rose to 5.2 because the above-grade parking structure had been left out of the calculation. It said units, parking and height are unchanged.
